Makes the response selection action menu the default in the Agents window by setting `chat.agentSessions.responseSelectionMenu.enabled` to `true`. Selecting assistant response text now shows the menu with **Ask in a Side Chat**, **Quote**, and **Copy** instead of the Ask Question input. The setting stays experiment-controlled (`experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`), so ExP assignments can still override the default.

The menu from #337472 was A/B tested in the Agents window and is being rolled out to all Agents window users.

The accessibility help test for the Ask Question input now sets the setting to `false` explicitly, since that is no longer the default.

## How to test

1. Remove any `chat.agentSessions.responseSelectionMenu.enabled` user setting. Note that an ExP assignment can still override the default.
2. In the Agents window, select text in an assistant response. The action menu appears with Ask in a Side Chat, Quote, and Copy.
3. Set `chat.agentSessions.responseSelectionMenu.enabled` to `false`. Selecting response text shows the Ask Question input again.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/responseSelectionSideChatController.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts`: passed (128 passing)
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p src/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: no errors in the changed files; the 409 diagnostics (missing Electron types in this local environment) are identical to `origin/main`

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window startup and chat-view creation with the response-selection menu now enabled by default
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration registration resolves a boolean default during contribution loading. Opening a chat constructs ResponseSelectionSideChatController, but that constructor already eagerly creates both FeedbackInputWidget and Menu regardless of the setting; the changed default is not read until a response selection is shown.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of open Agents chat views. Per view, controller, input, menu, actions, and listeners are unchanged before and after the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per-view UI construction is unchanged; no queue, limiter, or parallel expensive work is added by the default flip.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration lookup uses the existing configuration service. Cold and warm behavior are unchanged, and no new cache, cache key, miss, or retry behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff adds no startup CPU, allocation, I/O, IPC, subprocess, database, or network mechanism beyond resolving a different boolean constant.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact UI construction cost is not measured, but construction cardinality and objects are provably unchanged because both surfaces were already created unconditionally.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the changed default does not cause eager creation of the menu or add startup work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selecting assistant response text in an Agents chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A document selectionchange is scheduled to an animation frame, resolves the response selection, then shows and positions either the prebuilt menu or prebuilt input. The new default chooses the menu; both variants perform the same selection resolution, highlighting, geometry reads, and overlay positioning, while the old input path additionally autosized and updated its action state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Telemetry logs one response-selection 'shown' action with the selected variant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event when the affordance transitions from hidden to visible, unchanged from the old default; only the variant value changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same action was logged as askQuestionInput; after the diff it is logged as actionMenu.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing telemetry call occurs after the overlay surface is selected and does not add a new boundary to selection handling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One scheduled update per completed selection gesture, with scroll-driven repositioning only while the affordance is visible. Transcript size does not change the diff's cardinality because selection resolution and positioning are shared by both variants.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selection changes are coalesced by the existing AnimationFrameScheduler. The diff neither removes coalescing nor adds parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. The selected Range and last placement rectangles are retained only for the lifetime of the visible affordance under both variants.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing _applySelectionChange, _showFor, and _reposition that the changed default swaps prebuilt surfaces without increasing event frequency or collection-wide work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser layout costs vary by platform, but the shared positioning reads are unchanged and the newly selected menu path does not add a new repeated layout loop.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: there is no added synchronous UI-work mechanism, and the action-menu path avoids the old input autosizing calls on initial display.

Scenarios.Scenario: Using Ask in a Side Chat, Quote, or Copy from the newly default response-selection menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After selection, explicit user activation invokes the chosen action. Ask first opens the already-created input and only creates/opens/sends a side chat after a later explicit submission; Quote updates the local chat input; Copy performs a clipboard write.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/open/send a side chat through IChatSideChatService after the user chooses Ask and submits a question.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight request chain per controller because isBusy prevents duplicate submissions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With the old default, submitting the directly shown Ask Question input reached the same side-chat boundary; the menu adds an explicit Ask choice before that input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This boundary is on the explicit question-submit path, not response selection or menu display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write selected response text through IClipboardService after the user explicitly chooses Copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clipboard write per explicit Copy activation, independent of transcript item count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The operation already existed in the action-menu variant; the diff changes the default exposure but does not execute it automatically or increase calls per activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the Copy action waits for the clipboard write; selection and menu display do not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation per explicit action activation. Quote formatting scales linearly with selected text length, and clipboard bytes scale with selected text length; neither runs merely because the default changed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Side-chat submission remains one promise chain per explicit submit and blocks duplicate submission with the existing busy state. Clipboard writes are awaited per explicit click. The diff adds no burst or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. The selected response text is retained only while the affordance is open, unchanged from the enabled-menu behavior that already existed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from direct action-handler tracing that no network or clipboard boundary is executed by the changed default itself.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Selected text and side-chat latency can vary, but all expensive operations remain gated by explicit user actions and retain one-operation-per-action cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the newly default menu exposes intentional actions, but expensive boundaries remain explicit, bounded, and no more frequent per activation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening Sessions Chat accessibility help and running its updated tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessibility help synchronously reads the configuration boolean and appends one of two localized strings. The changed test explicitly supplies false to continue testing the legacy description.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per accessibility-help invocation and constant work per test case.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully synchronous string assembly; no added asynchronous work or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing localized strings and configuration service behavior are unchanged; no new cache state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed test and provider branch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the branch selects one constant string.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: only branch selection and test configuration changed, with constant CPU and allocation cost.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced all setting consumers. The PR changes which already-constructed response-selection surface is shown by default and updates a test fixture. It introduces no new eager allocation, hot-path multiplicity, unbounded retention, fan-out, concurrency burst, or expensive boundary, so no performance finding was submitted.
